objective: Establish the production extension-dependency guard, then extract a supported bounded-process and Git snapshot service boundary from pi-git, separating process supervision, collection, parsing, and rendering while preserving git_snapshot and /pi-git behavior and enabling pi-hud to consume stable contracts.

in: Add the production-source architecture check that rejects imports resolving beneath sibling extension private src trees, initially with exact stale-detecting exceptions only for current pi-hud violations.
Characterize current pi-git tool, command, cancellation, bounds, error, parsing, and rendering behavior.
Move bounded subprocess execution into a small package-level service without registration side effects.
Define a typed Git snapshot contract and separate collection/parsing from presentation.
Update pi-git adapters to use the supported service and export only the contract intended for sibling consumers.
Document the supported boundary and hand temporary guard exceptions to initiative 03 for mandatory removal.
out: Changing git_snapshot fields, /pi-git output semantics, timeouts, limits, or cancellation behavior.
Refactoring pi-hud itself or removing its temporary exceptions; initiative 03 owns consumer migration and final zero-allowlist enforcement.
Creating a general-purpose process framework or moving unrelated subprocess code.
Scanning test fixtures as production dependency violations.

constraints: Preserve public tool and command names and structured output compatibility.
Keep process execution bounded, cancellable, output-limited, and free of shell interpolation regressions.
Shared contracts and services must have no Pi registration or UI side effects.
The architecture check scans production extension source only; any initial exception must name the exact file/import, fail when stale, and be removed by initiative 03.
Do not duplicate context telemetry or artifact publication responsibilities.
Current source and tests must be inspected before edits; intentionally revise this authority if they invalidate its contract.

acceptanceCriteria.text: git_snapshot and /pi-git retain compatible outputs, bounds, cancellation, and structured error behavior.
Bounded process supervision is owned by a supported small service rather than pi-git's snapshot orchestration module.
Git collection and parsing are separated from rendering behind a typed snapshot contract usable without importing pi-git private src internals.
Focused and repository qualification passes, and documentation identifies the supported consumer boundary.

A production-source dependency check runs before service extraction, rejects new sibling private-src imports, and permits only exact stale-detecting temporary HUD exceptions owned for removal by initiative 03.

assessment.reason: The extension is narrow, but process cancellation, resource bounds, a new shared contract, and an early architecture guard affect downstream HUD decoupling and repository boundaries.
unknowns: The exact package-level filenames should follow existing repository conventions discovered during implementation.
Additional internal consumers of execBounded may need migration or explicit compatibility shims.

practices.reason: New sibling-private dependencies must be prevented before shared services begin moving.
Existing observable Git behavior must remain stable while internal responsibilities move.
Cancellation, output limits, parsing, and stable typed boundaries require direct negative and integration tests.
The extracted boundary must work across repository checks and be safe for later sibling consumption.

obligations.text: Verify the production-only architecture check rejects a new sibling private-src import, accepts current source only through exact temporary HUD exceptions, and fails when an exception is stale or broadened.
Run focused characterization tests before and after extraction for tool/command output, unusual Git states, cancellation, timeouts, output limits, and structured failures.
Verify the bounded-process service and Git contract have no registration side effects, parsing/rendering remain separated, and no production consumer needs a new private pi-git src import.

Run pi-git focused tests plus typecheck, dependency, performance, and repository gates, then obtain independent review of behavior preservation, bounds, cancellation, guard behavior, and contract design.

testing.approach: Add the production-source dependency rule first with negative fixtures and only exact stale-detecting exceptions for current HUD violations.
testing.reason: The consolidation plan requires stopping new coupling before extraction starts.

work.title: Characterize current pi-git behavior and define the stable contract

testing.approach: Add or strengthen focused tests around current snapshots, rendering, errors, cancellation, and bounds before moving code.
testing.reason: The refactor should preserve a proven behavioral baseline.

work.title: Extract bounded process and Git snapshot services

testing.approach: Move responsibilities behind typed package-level modules, update adapters, and run focused service and integration tests including negative process cases.
testing.reason: A small supported boundary removes de facto private API reuse without redesigning pi-git.

work.title: Document and qualify the pi-git service boundary

testing.approach: Run the complete declared gate set on current sources and request source-bound independent review.
testing.reason: Downstream initiatives need a qualified stable provider contract and enforced boundary.

decisions.text: pi-git owns Git collection and parsing; the shared process service owns only bounded execution mechanics.
decisions.basis: This preserves narrow domain ownership and avoids a shared-service monolith.

decisions.text: The initial dependency guard is delivered here before extraction; initiative 03 owns removal of the exact HUD exceptions.
decisions.basis: This matches the consolidation plan's ordering while preserving one clear migration owner.

decisions.text: No pi-git public redesign is included.
decisions.basis: The architecture review judges the extension basically good and recommends extraction rather than replacement.

risks.text: Moving process code changes cancellation or output-limit semantics.
risks.mitigation: Characterize those behaviors first and exercise timeout, abort, oversized-output, and shutdown cases after extraction.

risks.text: The new service becomes an unbounded general utility.
risks.mitigation: Keep its typed API minimal and scoped to existing proven bounded execution needs.
Require exact stale-detecting entries and make their removal an explicit initiative 03 completion criterion.
